question: What does % NRV mean?

what_it_means.text: Guidance on nutrition labelling from the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) describes nutrient reference values (NRVs) as guidelines about the amount of vitamins and minerals that it is recommended should be consumed on a daily basis in order to maintain a healthy diet.

Guidance on nutrition labelling from the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) says that when vitamins or minerals are declared on a food label, they must also be given as a percentage of their NRVs, in addition to the actual amounts.

Guidance on nutrition labelling from the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) says the NRVs for the vitamins and minerals that may be declared are set out in point 1 of Part A of Annex XIII of Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011 on the provision of food information to consumers.

Guidance on nutrition labelling from the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) says the European Commission's decision is that, on food labels, the generic term 'reference intakes' is used rather than NRVs.

what_it_doesnt_tell_you.text: A % NRV figure is worked out against the values listed in Annex XIII, not values for particular groups of people. Guidance on nutrition labelling from the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) says that from 13 December 2014 only the reference intakes listed in Annex XIII can be used, unless rules on reference intakes for specific population groups, such as children, are adopted.

what_the_evidence_says.text: Guidance on nutrition labelling from the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) says vitamins and minerals declared on a food label have to be present in 'significant amounts', which as a rule means 15% of the NRV per 100g or 100ml for products other than drinks, 7.5% of the NRV per 100ml for drinks, or 15% of the NRV per portion if the package contains only a single portion.

Guidance on nutrition labelling from the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) says the percentage of the NRV on a food label must be given per 100g or per 100ml, and may also be given per portion.

Guidance on food supplements from the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) says that if a supplement's recommended daily intake is 6 tablets, taken as 2 tablets 3 times a day, the amounts on the label should be given for the total daily intake.

notes: Sources, both from the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) and read live on 5 Nov 2026. TG: 'Technical guidance on nutrition labelling' (DHSC, Version 2, September 2016; GOV.UK publication updated 3 Mar 2017), PDF on assets.publishing.service.gov.uk. FS: 'Guidance notes on legislation implementing Directive 2002/46/EC on food supplements' (DHSC, GOV.UK HTML page, part of 'Food supplements: guidance and FAQs'). what_it_means: NRV definition (TG chapter VII, 'Nutrient reference values ("Reference intakes")', 'Definition of nutrient reference values'); mandatory % NRV alongside amounts (TG chapter VII, 'Mandatory information on percentages of NRVs'); Annex XIII Part A point 1 (TG chapter VII, 'Definition of nutrient reference values'; the regulation's full name from TG's introduction, where it is abbreviated EU FIC); 'reference intakes' term (TG chapter III, 'Provision of % reference intakes for vitamins and/or minerals', and the note in chapter VII). what_it_doesnt_tell_you: only Annex XIII values, no values for specific population groups (TG chapter VII, 'RIs for other "population groups" (e.g. children)'). what_the_evidence_says: significant amounts (TG chapter III, 'Declaration of vitamins and minerals: Significant amounts'); per 100g or 100ml, optionally per portion (TG chapter VII, 'Mandatory information on percentages of NRVs'); total daily intake (FS section 5.7, question on flexibility in expressing regulation 6(3)(c)). Food and supplements use the same reference values (legal check on legislation.gov.uk, 5 Nov 2026; legislation.gov.uk is not on the trusted list, so this is context, not a cited line): Directive 2002/46/EC Article 8(3) refers supplement percentages to the reference values in the Annex to Directive 90/496/EEC; Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011 Article 53 repeals Directive 90/496/EEC as from 13 December 2014 and says references to it are to be read as references to the Regulation; and regulation 6(3)(e) of the Food Supplements (England) Regulations 2003, as amended on 13 December 2014 by S.I. 2014/1855, requires a percentage of the relevant reference value in point 1 of Part A of Annex XIII. FS's FAQ on regulation 6(3)(e) still uses the older 'recommended daily allowance (RDA)' wording; no trusted source says RDA was the earlier term, so RDA is left out. TG is a 2016 to 2017 guide written before the UK left the EU and still refers to EU law and the European Commission.
